own_solution.law: RC charging: V_C(t) = V0 (1 - exp(-t/(R C))), tau = 0.1 s, V_C(80 ms) = 12 (1 - e^{-0.8})

TC3C7.regime: irrelevant while the opening time exceeds 80 ms

T821E.regime: irrelevant while the disconnection time exceeds 80 ms

notes: Checked certified answers: q = 1 kOhm: tau = 0.12 s, 12(1 - e^{-0.6667}) = 12 * 0.48658 = 5.83899 V; q = 2 kOhm: tau = 0.14 s, 5.22338 V; q = 5 kOhm: tau = 0.2 s, 12(1 - e^{-0.4}) = 3.95616 V. All match. K values 300, 500, 1000 ms all exceed 80 ms, so the answer stays 6.60805 V; the outside-regime expression V0(1 - exp(-q/tau)) is correct because an open-circuited ideal, non-leaking capacitor holds its voltage. Minimal pairs (T3BFD with T01DF, T97FD with TD847) state the same 2 kOhm and differ only in attachment; TC3C7 and T821E both state 500 ms. Agrees with my pass 1.
